title: Being ambitious and being a dad
titleZh: 雄心勃勃并成为一名父亲
author: nichochar
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Being ambitious and being a dad When I was going through YC, I didn’t mention my seven month old daughter to anyone. Now a few years later I have two kids, a dog and a very packed schedule. My kids are the best thing in my life. For years, my work was my life. Now my life competes with my work. I don’t think I’m alone. Here’s Paul Graham in Having Kids:

Some of my worries about having kids were right, though. They definitely make you less productive. I know having kids makes some people get their act together, but if your act was already together, you’re going to have less time to do it in.

I love building, learning, and competing. Life before kids was straightforward: I worked hard and centered my life around things I love: computers, technology, friends. I moved to SF, worked at some awesome companies, met a wonderful girl and built a strong relationship. A huge amount of my time was spent on work, and yet there was still some left for that and more. Turns out, you have a lot of time when you don’t have dependents. All the people I admire most are builders. I have devoured biographies and studied many great founders. Unfortunately this led me to an uncomfortable conclusion: most of them are horrible parents. Steve Jobs literally abandoned his daughter Lisa because “the time wasn’t right” (he was focused on Apple). Einstein abandoned one kid1 and was constantly absent, daydreaming about work around his other two, to the point where his wife divorced him and took them. Elon Musk has so many children and companies that he mechanically cannot spend any significant amount of time with any of them. Edison, Ford, Ferrari,… the list goes on and on. Most biographies of great founders I’ve read have had another story etched in between the lines: a pretty bleak one of a bad parent. I know many ambitious parents; it’s not an uncommon combination. Most of them are willing to make a choice that I will not: delegate the parenting away. I do not believe the quality time theory. I firmly believe in maximizing the quantity of time spent with them; there are no diminishing returns for them on that front. This is somewhat problematic, and unfortunately it gets worse. The time spent is even more important when they’re young, which of course happens to coincide with the prime of my career. I’ll find myself planning my work or reflecting on how much I accomplished today or in the last week and the result is clear. I’m a productive and well organized person, but comparing the output of parent-me to the kidless-me in a given week reveals a visible gap. Everyone knows life is short. Now that I have kids, it feels 10x shorter. This sucks. I am ambitious: I wake up every morning with a burning fire in my stomach to build awesome things. In this, I differ from Paul Graham:
I hate to say this, because being ambitious has always been a part of my identity, but having kids may make one less ambitious.

I am not less ambitious. But I am also ambitious about being a great dad. My anecdotal observations show a pretty strict dichotomy: great fathers and great achievers rarely overlap. Rarely is not never though. Some figures in technology (Paul Graham, DHH, Jeff Dean, even Mark Zuckerberg) seem to be pushing on both fronts with rare success. Often the pattern is early success, but not always. Frankly even if I couldn’t find the pattern, I would still not accept defeat. I don’t have a perfect magical solution. I’m voicing a frustration, but I am also rejecting the choice. I’ve come to redefine ambition for myself: ambition is being a great dad as well as building great things. I acknowledge and accept that it is much more difficult than just aiming for one or the other, and both are hard enough in their own right. But hard is the point of ambition, right? My strategy is pretty simple: stay focused, don’t waste time on bullshit, keep improving execution. I do this by carefully clarifying what I want my work to be, focusing on health to maximize energy, setting clear rules on time with kids (weekday dinners, weekends prioritize family) and completely removing time-wasting activities. With clear goals and discipline, my plan is to achieve compounding gains. I am writing this because I never hear anyone say it. Be ambitious enough to be an ambitious dad. Footnotes

I don’t think I’m alone. Here’s Paul Graham in Having Kids:

comments.author: marssaxman
comments.textRawHtml:
The passionate hunger to do something significant and meaningful with my life was a major reason I took care never to have any children. Having grown up in a large family within a religious subculture full of other large families, the amount of time and attention children consume was crystal clear from a young age, and I knew that I was going to need every scrap of energy I could spare for the work I wanted to do.

Years later, after I had to accept the failure of my ambitions, there was an opportunity to become the dad of a kid who needed one. So here I am being a dad after all, and it's been a good experience. Difficult, of course, and often frustrating, but worthwhile; I have no regrets - neither about this choice, nor the one I made when I was young.
comments.textZhHtml:
强烈渴望做一些对我的生活有意义的事情，这是我一直不生孩子的主要原因。我在一个充满其他大家庭的宗教亚文化的大家庭中长大，孩子们所消耗的时间和注意力从很小的时候起就水晶是显而易见的，我知道我将需要我能抽出的每一点精力来完成我想做的工作。

多年后，在我不得不接受我的雄心壮志的失败之后，有一个机会成为一个需要这个孩子的父亲。所以，我毕竟是一名父亲，这是一次很好的经历。当然，这很困难，而且常常令人沮丧，但还是值得的；我不后悔——无论是这个选择，还是我年轻时做出的选择。

children.author: Derbasti
children.textRawHtml:
> The passionate hunger to do something significant and meaningful with my life was a major reason I took care never to have any children.

Raising kids is probably the most meaningful and significant thing I have done with my life.
children.textZhHtml:
> 热衷于做一些有意义的事情是我一直不生孩子的主要原因。

抚养孩子可能是我一生中做过的最有意义的事情。

children.author: Gareth321
children.textRawHtml:
Agreed. I'm well travelled. Have had a very fun and satisfying dating life. A great career. Accomplished many life goals. Nothing comes close to fatherhood.

Which frustrates me immensely, because I feel that society at large did everything it could to convince me that parenthood is terrible. Movies and TV shows portrayed only the bad. Teachers told me that becoming a parent was the worst thing in the whole world. A wide range of celebrities spend their days posting about how amazing it is to be without children.

I accept that there are some parents out there who regret their decision, but research shows them to be a vanishingly small minority. The VAST majority of parents report greater meaning, more love, personal growth, enjoyment, fulfillment, etc. Something has become quite sick in modern society when we provide such an imbalanced and untrue message to young people.
children.textZhHtml:
同意。我旅行得很顺利。度过了非常有趣和令人满意的约会生活。一个伟大的职业生涯。完成了许多人生目标。没有什么比父亲身份更接近的了。

这让我非常沮丧，因为我觉得整个社会竭尽全力让我相信，为人父母是可怕的。电影和电视节目只描绘了不好的一面。老师告诉我，成为父母是世界上最糟糕的事情。许多名人整天都在发帖，讲述没有孩子的生活是多么令人惊奇。

我承认有些父母对他们的决定感到后悔，但研究表明他们只是极少数。绝大多数父母表示更有意义，更多的爱，个人成长，享受，成就感等。当我们向年轻人提供如此不平衡和不真实的信息时，现代社会的某些东西已经变得非常病态。

children.author: jraby3
children.textRawHtml:
I've thought about this and while I agree with you completely, I think the reason why is not just society at large. Externally what most people see is the time suck, money suck, and frustration with teaching behavior, fixing bad behavior etc.

What's so easy to miss is the immense feeling of love, of being needed, of being loved, that words can't describe. I frequently tell people I feel like the grinch after he discovers Xmas - my heart is three times bigger. But you can't really see that it's just a feeling I carry with me.
children.textZhHtml:
我思考过这个问题，虽然我完全同意你的观点，但我认为原因不仅仅是整个社会。从表面上看，大多数人看到的是浪费时间、浪费金钱，以及对教学行为、纠正不良行为等的挫败感。

很容易错过的是那种无法用言语描述的爱、被需要、被爱的巨大感觉。我经常告诉人们，在他发现圣诞节后，我感觉自己就像一个格林奇——我的心变大了三倍。但你看不出这只是我的一种感觉。

children.author: holy_eggplants
children.textRawHtml:
not only easy to miss but also hard to believe!

how do i explain that my child running into my arms after his first day of daycare is a high ill be chasing for the rest of my life? or the irrational pride when you see your kid flip over for the first time?

it's so many mundane moments that punch 100000x above their weight when its your kid having them. the good parts of parenting sound like fake news (unless youre talking to other parents)
children.textZhHtml:
不仅容易错过，而且难以相信！

我该如何解释我的孩子在托儿所第一天后跑到我怀里是我余生追逐的一个高病？ 或者当你第一次看到你的孩子翻身时的非理性骄傲？

有太多平凡的时刻，当你的孩子拥有它们时，它们的重量就超过了他们的体重 100000 倍。 养育子女的好部分听起来像是假新闻（除非你和其他父母交谈）

children.author: seanc
children.textRawHtml: Agree 100%.  I often tell expecting parents "All the hard stuff they tell you about; the sleep loss, the stress, the cost...  All that stuff is true.  But there's also all this amazing stuff they don't tell you about, which is also true."
children.textZhHtml: 100%同意。  我经常告诉准父母“他们告诉你的所有困难的事情；睡眠不足、压力、成本……所有这些都是真的。但也有他们没有告诉你的所有这些令人惊奇的事情，这也是事实。”

children.author: zingar
children.textRawHtml: I think that people probably tried to tell me about the amazing stuff, but I couldn't take it in. This created a very pleasant surprise for me when I found out about the good feels after the dread of just expecting everything I know to be upended with no reward.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为人们可能试图告诉我这些令人惊奇的东西，但我无法接受。当我在害怕期待我所知道的一切都被颠覆而没有任何回报后发现这种良好的感觉时，这给我带来了非常愉快的惊喜。

children.author: sneak
children.textRawHtml: You don’t need children to have these sorts of feelings, unless you can only get them from some small people who don’t have any choice but to love you.
children.textZhHtml: 你不需要孩子有这种感觉，除非你只能从一些除了爱你之外别无选择的小人物那里得到它们。

children.author: manmal
children.textRawHtml: There‘s a lot of ancient biology at play in raising kids. You won’t get exactly this kind of feeling elsewhere. Doesn’t mean it has to be your kids though. You just need to be an important part of their life.
children.textZhHtml: 许多古老的生物学因素在抚养孩子方面发挥着作用。在其他地方你不会有这种感觉。但这并不意味着它必须是你的孩子。您只需要成为他们生活中的重要组成部分即可。

children.author: marliechiller
children.textRawHtml: Do you have children? If no, then how can you make this assertion? If yes, what or who is filling the gap that children fill for you?
children.textZhHtml: 您有孩子吗？如果不是，那么你怎么能做出这样的断言呢？如果是，什么或谁正在填补孩子为您填补的空白？

children.author: siren2026
children.textRawHtml:
This is a fallacy. You don't need to live a situation to be able to comment about it.

Especially if we try to rationalize the choice. If you talk about "feelings", then fine. But be aware that "feelings" could simply be your hormone levels changing after having kids.
children.textZhHtml:
这是一个谬论。您无需经历某种情况才能对其发表评论。

特别是当我们尝试使选择合理化时。如果你说的是“感情”，那就好。但请注意，“感觉”可能只是生孩子后荷尔蒙水平的变化。

children.author: ido
children.textRawHtml: The feelings are definitely influences by hormones. Doesn't make them any less real.
children.textZhHtml: 感觉肯定是受荷尔蒙影响的。不会让它们变得不那么真实。

children.author: siren2026
children.textRawHtml:
Sure. But if you want a rationale discussion about what matters in life as this blog post and parent commenter suggest you probably don't want to get influenced by feelings.

There is a ton of philosophy written around this. Feelings are a very self-centric view of the world. The goal of rationalization is to take a wider systemic view without being self-centered.

Because if you push feelings and chemistry to the max you could also make an argument that taking meth and heroin is the most important thing in the world, as the feelings coming out of it are very real.
children.textZhHtml:
当然。但是，如果您想像这篇博文和家长评论者建议的那样就生活中重要的事情进行理性讨论，您可能不想受到感情的影响。

围绕这一点写了很多哲学。感情是一种非常以自我为中心的世界观。合理化的目标是采取更广泛的系统观点，而不是以自我为中心。

因为如果你将感受和化学反应发挥到极致，你也可以提出这样的论点：服用冰毒和海洛因是世界上最重要的事情，因为从中产生的感受是非常真实的。

children.author: the_af
children.textRawHtml:
Being a parent is in large part about feelings.

Also, the context of this conversation was replying to this assertion:

> You don’t need children to have these sorts of feelings

So it's about feelings, not about "rational discussion". Not a "fallacy" like you claimed, but the actual topic of discussion.
children.textZhHtml:
为人父母很大程度上是关于感受的。

而且，这次对话的背景是在回应这样的断言：

> 你不需要孩子有这样的感受

所以这是关于感受的，而不是关于“理性讨论”的。不是您声称的“谬论”，而是实际讨论的主题。

children.author: siren2026
children.textRawHtml:
This discussion is many level deeps based on a blog post that claims having kids is the most meaningful thing you can do with your life. And other grand similar statements.

>>> Raising kids is probably the most meaningful and significant thing I have done with my life.
children.textZhHtml:
此讨论基于一篇博客文章，内容涉及多个层面，该文章声称生孩子是您一生中可以做的最有意义的事情。以及其他类似的宏大陈述。

>>> 抚养孩子可能是我一生中做过的最有意义和最重要的事情。

children.author: Forgeties79
children.textRawHtml:
You don’t need to be a parent to be allowed to comment on or speculate about being a parent, but this is definitely one of those things you can’t guess at or estimate.

Until it is your kid in front of you you can’t know what you’ll feel as a parent. Maybe it’s all hormones and monkey brain, but that doesn’t make it any different.

Many people do not have that Hollywood Magic moment where “everything changed.” Some of my friends experienced this, some of them did not. None of us experienced what we thought we would.
children.textZhHtml:
你不需要成为父母才可以评论或猜测成为父母，但这绝对是你无法猜测或估计的事情之一。

除非你的孩子出现在你面前，你无法知道作为父母的感受。也许都是荷尔蒙和猴脑的原因，但这并没有什么不同。

很多人都没有经历过“一切都改变了”的好莱坞魔术时刻。我的一些朋友经历过这种情况，有些则没有。我们没有人经历过我们以为会发生的事情。

children.author: siren2026
children.textRawHtml:
Again, feeling should not matter that much in this discussion.

We are talking past each other because some/most parents in those discussion cannot get out of their self-centered view of the worlds based on "feelings". But if you make a claim that having a kid is the most important thing in the world, you should be able to substantiate that claim without going back to "feelings" that only you can feel.
children.textZhHtml:
再说一次，在这次讨论中，感觉不应该那么重要。

我们正在互相谈论，因为这些讨论中的一些/大多数父母无法摆脱基于“感觉”的以自我为中心的世界观。但如果你声称拥有孩子是世界上最重要的事情，你应该能够证实这一说法，而不必回到只有你才能感受到的“感受”。

children.author: the_af
children.textRawHtml:
> Again, feeling should not matter that much in this discussion.

Yes, they should. We are, after all, replying to the initial assertion that (and I quote) "you don’t need children to have these sorts of feelings [love, being needed, needing someone]".

> But if you make a claim that having a kid is the most important thing in the world

That wasn't a claim anybody made in this thread, and specifically everyone was talking from a personal perspective about parenthood, not making universal claims. Certainly not the person who wrote this (and to whom you indirectly replied):

> What's so easy to miss is the immense feeling of love, of being needed, of being loved, that words can't describe. I frequently tell people I feel like the grinch after he discovers Xmas - my heart is three times bigger. But you can't really see that it's just a feeling I carry with me.

If you don't like talking about feelings, fine. But this discussion was about feelings, not about some universal "most important thing in the world".
children.textZhHtml:
> 再次强调，在本次讨论中，感觉不应该那么重要。

是的，他们应该如此。毕竟，我们是在回应最初的断言（我引用）“你不需要孩子有这些感觉[爱、被需要、需要某人]”。

> 但是，如果你声称拥有孩子是世界上最重要的事情

那不是任何人在这个帖子中提出的主张，特别是每个人都从个人角度谈论为人父母，而不是做出普遍的主张。当然不是写这篇文章的人（以及你间接回复的人）：

> 很容易错过的是那种无法用言语描述的爱、被需要、被爱的巨大感觉。我经常告诉人们，在他发现圣诞节后，我感觉自己就像一个格林奇——我的心变大了三倍。但你看不出这只是我随身携带的一种感觉。

如果你不喜欢谈论感觉，那好吧。但这次讨论是关于感受的，而不是关于某种普遍存在的“世界上最重要的事情”。

children.author: the_af
children.textRawHtml:
> You don't need to live a situation to be able to comment about it.

In the case of being a parent, yes, yo do. This is not something you can experience second-hand.
children.textZhHtml:
> 您不需要经历某种情况才能发表评论。

就作为父母而言，是的，您可以。这不是你可以二手体验的东西。

children.author: siren2026
children.textRawHtml:
Agree.

Remember that once you have kids you are stuck in that situation forever. There is a lot of coping and trying to persuade yourself that this is the best thing in the world. It might as well be as there is no escape anyways!
children.textZhHtml:
同意。

记住，一旦你有了孩子，你就会永远陷入这种境地。有很多应对方法，并试图说服自己这是世界上最好的事情。反正也无处可逃！
